results.title: Savannah's Great Dane wins Chinese tariff battle - The Current
results.content: After the ITC determined that the U.S. trailer manufacturers have been materially injured by imports, the Commerce Department last week instructed customs authorities to add duties ranging from 82.3% to 128.7% for trailers from China and 1.9% to 1.95% for trailers from Mexico. [...] U.S. customs officials are poised to levy new duties on semitruck trailers made in China and Mexico after a yearlong legal battle fought by Savannah’s Great Dane LLC and two other American manufacturers of this essential component of the trucking industry. [...] In a second decision, the Department of Commerce set additional duties on specific Chinese companies intended to offset the amount by which a product is sold at less than fair value — or “dumped” — in America.. Those antidumping duties were set at 130% in a preliminary decision that is expected to be finalized later this summer.

results.title: The Impact of Tariffs on Logistics - Transload Distribution Association of North America
results.content: As tariffs ripple through the supply chain, operational costs are rising across the board. Businesses are being forced to hold more inventory to buffer against delays and price volatility, increasing demand for warehouse space and driving up storage costs. [...] Tariffs are significantly disrupting supply chains, particularly those dependent on just-in-time (JIT) systems. Increased customs scrutiny and regulatory complexity are slowing clearance times at ports, creating bottlenecks and delays. [...] The implementation of tariffs has created a ripple effect across the global logistics industry, transforming a system once defined by efficiency and predictability into one characterized by volatility and complexity. Rising costs, shifting trade lanes, and ongoing policy changes have forced businesses to rethink traditional supply chain strategies.
